name: OWASP Mobile Application Security Verification Standard (MASVS)
source_notes: Control IDs and statements verified from OWASP_MASVS.yaml in a clone of OWASP/masvs (last commit 2026-09-21); version/date from the MASVS releases page (summarized fetch).
caveats: MASVS controls have no short titles; name holds the official one-sentence control statement verbatim and summary paraphrases it.
v2.1.0 (2024-01-18) added MASVS-PRIVACY; v2.0.0 (2023-04-01) removed L1/L2/R levels. v2.1.0 as latest rests on a summarized releases page; no v2.2/v3 was found in repo files.
maswe arrays invert MASWE masvs-v2 front-matter mappings captured in the notes; controls whose MASWE mappings were not captured have empty arrays (e.g. AUTH, CODE-1/2, RESILIENCE-1/2).
mastg_tests are derived via MASTG test -> MASWE -> MASVS; MASTG tests whose MASWE link was not recorded (e.g. 0209, 0210, 0317, 0388) are omitted.
Mobile Top 10 2024 links are inferred; OWASP publishes no MASVS-to-Top-10 mapping.
detection.static is the union of the linked MASWE signals (reinhardt rule ideas).
Maturity 'flagship' is that of the OWASP MAS project (level 4).

items.name: The app securely stores sensitive data.
items.summary: Sensitive data the app stores is protected at rest.
prevention: Store secrets and tokens in the platform keystore (Keychain on iOS, Keystore on Android) rather than UserDefaults or AsyncStorage.
In React Native/Expo use expo-secure-store or react-native-keychain for tokens and secrets.
Do not hardcode API keys or put private values in EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables.

static: UserDefaults.standard.set(...) or @AppStorage("...token|password|secret|apiKey...") holding secrets instead of Keychain
FileManager / POSIX I/O / Core Data / SQLite writes of sensitive data without encryption
React Native AsyncStorage.setItem(...) with token/secret-like keys (AsyncStorage is unencrypted)
Sensitive data written to shared storage or shared App Group containers without encryption
Raw key literals passed to SecKeyCreateWithData, CCCrypt key parameter, or CryptoKit init(rawRepresentation:) (e.g. P256.Signing.PrivateKey)
API keys or secret literals in Swift string constants or Info.plist
EXPO_PUBLIC_* variable names containing SECRET, PRIVATE, SERVICE_ROLE or a non-publishable KEY
